profile_text.body:
The Alan Turing Institute is a nonprofit organization headquartered in London, United Kingdom. Its site describes its mission as changing the world using data science and artificial intelligence, and says it works with a wide range of partners to deliver that mission. It publishes Turing News and Turing Events, and points readers to CETaS and Skills at the Turing.

The site describes several areas of AI work. The Defence AI Research Centre (DARe) is described as providing strategic advantage for UK Defence and National Security, partnering with government, industry and academia on novel AI technologies. Project Bluebird is described as work on ways AI systems can benefit air traffic control, including digital twins of UK airspace to forecast aircraft behaviour and trajectories. Other items include Aemelia, described as AI-enabled satellite morphological inference from multidimensional inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) data, open-source infrastructure for argument-based AI assurance, and AI forecasting combined with expert knowledge and climate context to extend the range of predictions. The site names Isabel Fenton, who it says applies data science and AI to environmental challenges such as biodiversity loss and renewable energy generation, and Carlos Gavidia-Calderon, a research software engineer whose work it describes as ranging from the ethics of machine learning to digital twins of hearts.

The institute's profile lists it as a nonprofit based in London. No products, litigation, or MCP servers are associated with it in the available material.
